## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics
- Date: Not provided in supplied source material
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cJ2QCyr3yzU
  Summary: A repeatable `Claude Co-work` operating pattern: create a dedicated local workspace, split it into `context`, `projects`, and `output`, then preload persistent instruction files such as `aboutme.md`, `brandvoice.md`, and `workingpreferences.md`. The source describes using this for inbox triage, daily topic research, task management, and personal tracking.
  Why it matters: The core tactic is persistent local context, which reduces prompt churn and makes file-based work more repeatable.
  Tools/models: Claude desktop `Co-work`; optional connectors such as Gmail, Google Calendar, and Notion.
  Setup: 1. Install Claude desktop. 2. Create a parent workspace and the three subfolders. 3. Add the three markdown context files. 4. Configure global instructions in Co-work. 5. Point recurring tasks at that workspace.
  Available now: Source describes it as currently available on Claude desktop.

- Date: Not provided in supplied source material
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SNo_recKZyY
  Summary: A document-operations workflow for turning multiple client meeting transcripts into finished deliverables. The source describes dropping several transcript files into a project folder, then having `Co-work` generate one spreadsheet-style project tracker and one short follow-up email per client, with tasks, owners, deadlines, and priorities extracted from the calls.
  Why it matters: This is a direct admin-ops compression workflow: unstructured call text in, structured project artifacts out.
  Tools/models: Claude desktop `Co-work`; local transcript files; spreadsheet/document outputs.
  Setup: 1. Save transcripts in the `projects` folder. 2. Prompt Co-work to process all files and save results to `output`. 3. Review extracted deadlines, owners, and client-specific follow-up text before use.
  Available now: Source describes it as currently available via Co-work.

- Date: Not provided in supplied source material
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDGiWn0flK8
  Summary: An outcome-first `Claude Code` workflow for variable tasks. The source frames the tactic as specifying the end state rather than building a deterministic node-by-node automation, then letting the agent ask clarifying questions, choose steps, and iterate toward the deliverable.
  Why it matters: Useful for work that is too variable for rigid automation graphs, especially research, content operations, and support-style tasks.
  Tools/models: VS Code plus Claude Code.
  Setup: 1. Install VS Code. 2. Open Claude Code. 3. State the desired output and constraints, not the full implementation plan. 4. Answer clarifying questions. 5. Review artifacts and tighten instructions on reruns.
  Available now: Source describes it as currently available.
